key_definitions.definition: A statistical graph used to display the frequency distribution of categorical data, using vertical bars.
Data generated by a categorical variable, and where the data values are the names of categories.
Variables that classify or name a quality or attribute, and which generate data values which are the names of categories. Categorical variables are either nominal or ordinal.
Numerical data that can take any value, sometimes in an interval, and often arises from measuring.
Information collected about a variable.
Data which only take particular numerical values, usually whole numbers, and often arises from counting.
A variable which generates discrete numerical data, such as the number of people in a queue.
The number of times a value or a group of values occurs in a data set. Sometimes known as the count.
A listing of the values that a variable takes in a data set along with how often (frequently) each value occurs. Frequency can also be recorded as a percentage. G
The category or data interval that occurs most frequently in a data set.
The most frequently occurring value in a data set. There may be more than one.
A type of categorical data where data values are the names of groups.
A type of categori- cal variable where the values of the variable are the names of groups.

Data obtained by measuring or counting some quantity. Numerical data can be discrete (for example, the number of people waiting in a queue) or continuous (for example, the amount of time people spent waiting in a queue). O
A type of categorical data where the values of the variable are the names of groups, and there is an inherent order in the categories.
A type of categori- cal variable where when the values of the variable are the names of groups, and there is an inherent order in the categories.
Frequency of a value or group of values, expressed as a percentage of the total frequency.
